column1: # G1m (2026-10-30, the user: "try with the same amount of modes we give the main recons ... 8 modes, and see if it
# becomes a convolution"): G1 / G1b's lone Pb atom, the same sims (reused; no new simulation), reconstructed with the
# probe RELEASED as 8 modes started from each sim's own mixed state -- the campaign's mode-leg recipe (mono300 _mixF:
# PROBE_MIXED, probe update from iteration 40 / 20, aperture constraint, 250 iterations). Run with
#   PROBE_MODES=8 NITER=250 bash runs/zb_submit.sh runs/g1m.tsv        (RTAG defaults to _m8)
# Three outcomes, read against G1 / G1b's fixed-probe kernels and the deconvolution test (analysis/deconv_test.py):
#   the reconstruction returns to the nothing-added atom  -> the modes take the blur into the beam (what mixed-state
#                                                            ptychography is for: Thibault & Menzel 2013)
#   it matches the smear of the nothing-added atom        -> with modes the blur IS a convolution
#   it stays as lossy as with the fixed probe             -> 8 modes do not capture it
# The coherent points are the controls: what releasing the probe with 8 modes does to an atom with nothing added.
# Phonon points are left out: the old sims moved the atom sqrt(3) too far, and new ones (_T<T>v2) need ptychoshelves'
# sigma fix pulled on Blythe first (zb_submit refuses them without it). For a lone atom, moving the atom equals moving
# the probe, so vibration is a source + focal spread of the atom's own rms; the source and focal-spread points below
# speak for it until then.
